new_leaves.label: Paleo-Indian Fluted Points
new_leaves.defn: The flaked stone projectile points of the Paleo-Indian period of North America (c. 13,000–8,000 BCE): Clovis, Folsom, Gainey, Cumberland and other fluted points, then the parallel-flaked lanceolate points of the Plano complexes (Agate Basin, Hell Gap, Cody, Scottsbluff), knapped from chosen jasper, chert, chalcedony and obsidian with a care for symmetry, colour and the full-length flute beyond any need of use.
new_leaves.aliases: Clovis points; Folsom points; Fluted points; Paleoindian projectile points
catalogues: Clovis points in the British Museum
new_leaves.axis: types and phases, then holding institutions
kinds: unfluted lanceolate points of the late Paleo-Indian Plains

new_leaves.label: Nyau Masks
new_leaves.defn: The masks and costumes of the Nyau society of the Chewa of Malawi, Zambia and Mozambique, danced in the Gule Wamkulu ('great dance') at initiations, funerals and commemorations: carved and painted wooden face masks of spirits, animals and caricatured figures, and large basketry and straw structures; inscribed by UNESCO in 2005.
src: British Museum, Endangered Material Knowledge Programme
catalogues: Nyau masks in the British Museum
Chewa objects in the Metropolitan Museum
new_leaves.axis: types and phases, then holding institutions
kinds: Kungoni Centre of Culture and Art, Malawi

new_leaves.label: Vigango
new_leaves.defn: Carved wooden memorial posts (singular kigango) of the Mijikenda of coastal Kenya, two to three metres tall, erected for deceased members of the Gohu society by the Giriama, Kauma, Jibana, Chonyi, Kambe and Ribe; incarnations of ancestors that may not be removed, many since returned from foreign museums.
catalogues: Mijikenda objects in the Metropolitan Museum
National Museum of African Art: Mijikenda
vigango and Mijikenda objects at the Smithsonian
new_leaves.axis: types and phases, then holding institutions
kinds: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art
